{{Short description|American biologist and poet (1934–2024)}}
{{Sources|date=February 2025}}
[[File:Myra Sklarew 1144396.jpg|thumb|Myra Sklarew]]

'''Myra Weisberg Sklarew'''<ref>{{cite book |url=https://jscholarship.library.jhu.edu/bitstream/handle/1774.2/36803/commencement1970.pdf |article=Masters of Arts in the Faculty of Arts and Sciences |title=Conferring of Degrees at the close of the ninety-fourth academic year |date=May 27, 1970 |page=47 |publisher=The Johns Hopkins University |location=Baltimore, Maryland |accessdate=2020-11-04}}</ref> (December 18, 1934 – December 30, 2024) was an American biologist, poet and teacher.

==Life and career==
Sklarew was born in Baltimore, Maryland in 1934.<ref name=":0" /> She began writing poetry at the age of 7 or 8, in part because of her frequent long stays at home due to reoccurring [[Streptococcal pharyngitis|strep throat]] infections.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Smith |first=Harrison |date=29 January 2025 |title=Myra Sklarew, meditative poet and writing teacher, dies at 90 |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/obituaries/2025/01/29/myra-sklarew-dead/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250130140538/https://www.washingtonpost.com/obituaries/2025/01/29/myra-sklarew-dead/ |archive-date=30 January 2025 |access-date=30 January 2025 |work=[[The Washington Post]]}}</ref>

She received a biology degree from [[Tufts University]], in 1956. She studied [[bacterial genetics]] and [[bacterial virus]]es with [[Salvador Luria]] and [[Max Delbrück]] at the [[Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory]].<ref name=":0" /> In 1961, she moved to [[Bethesda, Maryland]] with her family. She later studied with Elliott Coleman at the [[Johns Hopkins University]] Writing Seminars, where she received an [[Master of Arts|M.A.]] in 1970.  After that, she began teaching at [[American University]], and taught there from 1970 to 2007, except for a four-year stint, from 1987 to 1991, where she served as president of the [[Yaddo|Yaddo artist community]].<ref name=":0" />

Sklarew was the author of three [[chapbook]]s, and six collections of poetry. Her poems are in the Contemporary Poets Archive at the [[Library of Congress]], while her papers are in the [[University of Maryland]] Archives.<ref>{{cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Myra Sklarew papers|url=https://archives.lib.umd.edu/repositories/2/resources/111|archive-url=|archive-date=|accessdate=|website=|publisher=University of Maryland Special Collections and University Archives}}</ref> 

After her retirement in 2007, Sklarew was emerita professor of literature in the writing program at American University. 

Sklarew died due to complications from [[Crohn's disease|Crohn’s disease]] on December 30, 2024, at the age of 89.<ref name=":0" />

*''A survivor named trauma: Holocaust memory in Lithuania'' ([[SUNY Press]], ''forthcoming'')
*''If You Want to Live Forever'' Chapbook, 2012, in Ashes Caught on the Edge of Light, Winterhawk Press

*''The Journey of Child Development: Selected Papers of Dr. Joseph Nospitz'', Routledge, 2010, co-editor with Bruce Sklarew
*[https://books.google.com/books?id=Rd1zGX1pj8kC&q=myra+sklarew ''Over the Rooftops of Time: Jewish Stories, Essays, Poems''] ([[SUNY Press]], 2002) {{ISBN|9780791455753}}
*[https://books.google.com/books?id=ZxM1fELXgHcC&q=myra+sklarew ''The Witness Trees: Poetry and Essays''] ([[Cornwall Books]], 2000) {{ISBN|9780845348901}}
*''Lithuania: New & Selected Poems'' (Azul Editions, 1995, 1997), {{ISBN|9781885214027}}
*''Like a Field Riddled by Ants'' ([[Lost Road Publishers]], 1987), {{ISBN|9780918786364}}
*''Altamira'' ([[Washington Writers Publishing House]], 1987), {{ISBN|9780931846304}}
*''The Travels of the Itinerant Freda Aharon,'' Watermark Press, 1985 (chapbook)
*''The Science of Goodbyes'' (University of Georgia Press, 1982), {{ISBN|9780820306032}}
*''From the Backyard of the Diaspora'' (Dryad Press, 1981), {{ISBN|9780931848407}}
*''In The Basket of the Blind'' ([[Cherry Valley Editions]], 1975)
